The primary finding is that InMotion's initial entry targets a compiler-synthetic UnspecifiedInitial state rather than the NL-required Accelerating state, rendering all three operating substates (Accelerating, Cruising, Approaching) unreachable from root. issues.reason: The contract requires a state_action 'Emergency Stop' on EmergencyStopping. The FCSTM has a single during action with a merged compound name. The NL segment says 'includes the actions Emergency Stop' without specifying a lifecycle phase (entry/do/exit), so S4 cannot be invoked. The semantic content 'EmergencyStop' is present as a prefix of the merged name. S4 is unavailable because the NL does not supply an explicit lifecycle phase (it says 'includes the actions' without specifying entry/do/exit).

issues.strongest_rebuttal: The PlantUML 'send' annotation is a state-level signal emission that the compiler legitimately projects into the abstract lifecycle action. issues.basis: NL5 text; closed_model_inventory transition:line:18 source=[*] target=UnspecifiedInitial scope=InMotion; working_contract compiler:state:...UnspecifiedInitial kind=synthetic_state; verify_facts initial-entry:transition:line:18 proved (confirms edge exists but to wrong target); exact_source_inventory InMotion has no initial transition row.
issues.expected: The InMotion composite's initial pseudostate edge targets the Accelerating substate, so that system entry into InMotion activates the acceleration phase.
issues.observed: The InMotion composite's only initial edge (transition:line:18) targets UnspecifiedInitial (state:UnspecifiedInitial:line:17), a compiler-synthetic state. No [*]->Accelerating edge exists in the InMotion scope transition inventory.
issues.reason: NL5 requires InMotion's initial entry to target Accelerating. The complete InMotion-scope transition inventory (12 transitions) contains no [*]->Accelerating edge. The only initial edge targets the compiler-synthetic UnspecifiedInitial state. This is the root cause of all downstream unreachability and event-consumer-coverage failures.
issues.requirement_quote: The system begins in the Accelerating substate
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The source PlantUML simply omits an explicit initial edge within InMotion; the compiler filled the gap with a synthetic UnspecifiedInitial state. The author's intent was Accelerating as the default entry, and the defect is the absence of an explicit edge in the source rather than a positive misdirection. The synthetic state is a compiler artifact, not an author-specified operating state.
issues.title: InMotion initial entry targets UnspecifiedInitial instead of Accelerating

issues.basis: verify_facts reachability:refuted for state:Accelerating:line:10, state:Cruising:line:13, state:Approaching:line:14; inspection_equivalent_facts reachable_state_refs=[root, DoorsClosing, InMotion, UnspecifiedInitial, EmergencyStopping, Stopping] excludes all three; diagnostics STATE_UNREACHABLE_FROM_INITIAL for lines 10, 13, 14.
issues.expected: All three InMotion operating substates (Accelerating, Cruising, Approaching) are reachable from the root initial state, enabling the specified motion-phase behavior to execute.
issues.observed: None of the three substates is reachable from root. The InMotion composite is entered but routes to UnspecifiedInitial; the only reachable InMotion child is the compiler-synthetic state. verify_facts confirm reachability:refuted for all three.
issues.reason: NL5 establishes that the system begins in Accelerating and proceeds through motion phases. The deterministic reachability facts show all three operating substates are unreachable from root, meaning the entire specified motion-phase behavior (acceleration, cruising, approaching) can never execute in the closed model.
issues.requirement_quote: The system begins in the Accelerating substate, moving to the Cruising substate once cruising speed is reached, as indicated by the "Reached Cruising/Cruise" signal.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The unreachability is entirely caused by the single initial-entry defect (the missing [*]->Accelerating edge). Fixing that one edge would make all three substates reachable via the existing internal transitions (Accelerating->Cruising, Accelerating->Approaching, Cruising->Approaching). The substates themselves are correctly declared and internally connected.
issues.title: InMotion operating substates unreachable from root initial entry

issues.basis: verify_facts event-consumer:Reached_Cruising_Cruise status=refuted (consumer_transition_refs=[transition:line:19], reachable_consumer_transition_refs=[]); event-consumer:Approached_Decelerate status=refuted (consumer_transition_refs=[transition:line:20, transition:line:21], reachable_consumer_transition_refs=[]); inspection_equivalent_facts diagnostics EVENT_CONSUMER_UNREACHABLE for both events.
issues.expected: Events Reached_Cruising_Cruise and Approached_Decelerate each have at least one reachable consumer transition within the InMotion operating scope, so that the specified phase transitions can be triggered at runtime.
issues.observed: Both events have declared consumers (Reached_Cruising_Cruise: transition:line:19; Approached_Decelerate: transitions:line:20, line:21) but zero reachable consumers. The only reachable InMotion child state is UnspecifiedInitial, which does not consume these events.
issues.reason: NL5, NL6, and NL7 specify that phase transitions are triggered by specific signals. The closed model shows no reachable consumer for Reached_Cruising_Cruise or Approached_Decelerate within InMotion, meaning these events are operationally dead even though they are declared and have consumer transitions. This is a distinct behavioral property from reachability: it concerns whether the event-response mechanism functions at runtime.
issues.requirement_quote: The system begins in the Accelerating substate, moving to the Cruising substate once cruising speed is reached, as indicated by the "Reached Cruising/Cruise" signal.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The events Arrived_Stop_Send_Arrived and Obstacle_Detected DO have reachable consumers via UnspecifiedInitial (transitions:line:28, line:29), so the InMotion composite is not entirely inert. The phase-transition events are blocked, but the termination events still function. Additionally, if the initial-entry defect is fixed, all consumers become reachable and this property is satisfied.
issues.title: Motion-phase events have no reachable consumers in InMotion scope

issues.basis: NL2 text; transition group NL-GROUP-NL2-TRANS ALT-NL2-STOPPING event=Arrived; closed_model_inventory transition:line:35 triggers=[] guard='R45RouteToken == 6'; event:Arrived_Stop_Send_Arrived:line:6 declared; working_contract compiler:route_control:R45RouteToken kind=route_control_variable.

issues.observed: Transition:line:35 has triggers=[] and guard='R45RouteToken == 6'. The event Arrived_Stop_Send_Arrived is declared in the model (event:Arrived_Stop_Send_Arrived:line:6) but is not present as a trigger on this transition.
issues.reason: The NL and transition group specify that the Arrived/Stop, Send Arrived signal triggers the InMotion-to-Stopping transition. The closed model's transition has an empty trigger set and relies on a variable guard instead. The trigger_set property as stated in the NL is not satisfied by the model's structural representation.
issues.requirement_quote: In the InMotion state, the system can either transition to the Stopping state when it arrives, indicated by the "Arrived/Stop, Send Arrived" signal, or to the EmergencyStopping state if an obstacle is detected.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The compiler uses a route-token lowering mechanism: child transitions within InMotion set R45RouteToken=6 when Arrived fires, and the parent transition InMotion->Stopping fires when the guard R45RouteToken==6 is satisfied. The event semantics are preserved through this two-step mechanism, and the transition is operationally equivalent to an event-triggered one from the system's external perspective.
issues.title: InMotion-to-Stopping transition lacks required Arrived event trigger
